title: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx + b for a line that crosses the y-axis at b

sections.skill: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx + b for a line that crosses the y-axis at b

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx + b for a line that crosses the y-axis at b
questions.prompt: A line has a slope of 2 and crosses the y-axis at (0, 3). Use a slope triangle from (0, 3) to a point (x, y) on the line (x ≠ 0) to explain why y = 2x + 3.
questions.prompt_markup:
A line has a slope of 2 and crosses the y-axis at (0, 3).
Use a slope triangle from (0, 3) to a point (x, y) on the line (x ≠ 0) to explain why y = 2x + 3.
questions.correct_answer: The slope triangle has run x and rise y - 3, so (y - 3) ÷ x = 2. Then y - 3 = 2x and y = 2x + 3. The point (0, 3) also fits.

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx + b for a line that crosses the y-axis at b
questions.prompt: The line y = mx is translated b units up. Explain why the image is the line y = mx + b.
questions.prompt_markup:
The line y = mx is translated b units up.
Explain why the image is the line y = mx + b.
questions.correct_answer: Each point (x, mx) moves to (x, mx + b), so every point of the image satisfies y = mx + b.

questions.correct_answer: y = 2x - 2 (the slope triangle has run 5 and rise 10)

questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Explain why every point (x, y) on the line through (2, 5) with a slope of 3 satisfies (y - 5) ÷ (x - 2) = 3 when x ≠ 2.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why every point (x, y) on the line through (2, 5) with a slope of 3 satisfies (y - 5) ÷ (x - 2) = 3 when x ≠ 2.
questions.correct_answer: The slope triangle from (2, 5) to (x, y) has run x - 2 and rise y - 5; every slope triangle on the line gives the same ratio, 3.

questions.skill: Describe vertical and horizontal translations of linear functions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x and g(x) = f(x) + 4. Write g(x), and describe how the graph of g compares with the graph of f.
questions.prompt_markup:
f(x) = 2x and g(x) = f(x) + 4.
Write g(x), and describe how the graph of g compares with the graph of f.
questions.correct_answer: g(x) = 2x + 4; the graph of f is translated 4 units up.

questions.prompt_markup:
f(x) = 2x and h(x) = f(x - 3).
Write h(x) in slope-intercept form, and describe the translation.
questions.correct_answer: h(x) = 2x - 6; the graph of f is translated 3 units right (which, for this line, is the same as 6 units down).
